subject: Shiny server - versions, problems with libraries, etc.

messages.author: 5117fd6c9c423ce1
messages.subject: Shiny server - versions, problems with libraries, etc.
parts:
Hi folks -

I'm trying to release a new Shiny app on my Shiny server, which has been working great, and has been version v0.3.6 installed from source on CentOS 6.2.  Now I have a new app which uses rgdal/gdal libraries (geospatial stuff).  The libraries I require for this app are recognized and found readily by R 3.0 on the very same machine as Shiny server.  However, when I go to start my app on the web from the server, I get an error telling me the libraries for rgdal cannot be found!   Yet R finds them?  I am confused what is going on, here.  isn't Shiny server using my installed version of R??  And, should I be upgrading my version of Shiny server, by the way?    How is the latest release different from 3.6?

thanks.

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Shiny server - versions, problems with libraries, etc.
parts:
I'm guessing when you run R on the Shiny Server machine and see that those libraries are there, you're running as your usual user account, and thus those libraries are in your personal library (~/R/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu-library/3.0 or something). By default, Shiny Server launches R under the "shiny" user account. You need to either install those packages for everyone, or for the shiny user account.

If you have "sudo" access on the machine, you can do this to install for everyone:

sudo su - -c "R -e \"install.packages('rgdal', repos='http://cran.rstudio.com/')\""

Or this to install as the shiny user:

sudo su - shiny -c R
(then from the R prompt:)
install.packages('rgdal', repos='http://cran.rstudio.com/')
